reasoning: The evidence shows that only 8 countries have ever won the World Cup: Brazil, Italy, Germany, Argentina, France, Spain, England, and Uruguay. The 2026 tournament features 48 teams (expanded from 32), with several first-time qualifiers (Curaçao, Cape Verde, Jordan, Uzbekistan). However, the favorites remain the traditional powerhouses: Argentina (defending champion), Spain (Euro 2024 champions), France, England, Brazil, and Germany. While the expanded format increases unpredictability, the evidence consistently identifies these 8 traditional winners as the main contenders. No emerging nation is mentioned as a serious favorite to win. The probability of a first-time winner depends on whether an underdog can overcome the established elite, which historically is rare despite the larger field.
